messages:
Jordan: FYI customer ACME (acct ac-889) reported ~30s of 429s during a short global fan-out. They say burst credits should have covered it. Logs attached below.
Maria: Do we know if they used one API key across regions or multiple keys? Burst buckets differ by what?
Alex: Single API key, same key used from both eu-west-1 and us-east-1 Lambdas. Traffic was a spike from a webhook fan-out + retries. Example request pattern: 200 reqs over 45s distributed ~60% EU / 40% US.
ACME-support: Repro steps: 1) PUT to /v1/predict concurrent 200 reqs over 45s from two regions 2) Observe ~30s of 429s then auto-recovery. We have a short capture: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/predict &
done
wait
```
Jordan: pasted service logs show a couple of lines like: 
```
2026-06-12T15:42:10Z request_id=... region=eu-west-1 token=ac-889 status=429 reason=burst_cushion_exhausted
2026-06-12T15:42:12Z request_id=... region=us-east-1 token=ac-889 status=429 reason=burst_cushion_exhausted
```
Cheng: Interesting — our burst credit model is per-account *and* sharded by region/availability-zone for capacity isolation, so parallel regional bursts can consume multiple sub-buckets faster than expected. Docs could be clearer about multi-region fan-outs.
Maria: Also check smoothing window and the refill granularity. If two regional streams align, the effective instantaneous draw can overshoot smoothing thresholds even when total long-term credit is available. We saw this with fractional refill math (60s window, refill tick 1s).
Alex: Can we recommend a quick mitigation for the customer? They want a change they can make without infra changes.
Maria: Short-term mitigations: 1) Add small randomized jitter on retry backoff (50-300ms) to avoid alignment. 2) Reduce concurrent per-region concurrency (split across time slices). 3) If they can, route more traffic to a single region for that spike so it consumes only one sub-bucket.
Cheng: Operational options from our side: a) Temporarily increase burst cushion for that account for 1 hour (manual top-up) b) Adjust smoothing config to allow a slightly higher instantaneous headroom during a rollout window — requires infra change and PM approval.
Jordan: I proposed a temporary top-up. InfraBot, can you open a short-lived credit top-up approval runbook for ac-889?
InfraBot: Created ticket INF-2043: "temporary-burst-topup ac-889" assigned to @chris-infra, ETA 2h.
Maria: For longer term: docs changes + an FAQ entry about multi-region burst semantics. Also let's add a short example repro in docs showing fan-out case and recommended client jitter.
Alex: I'll send ACME the jitter + concurrency suggestions and offer the temporary top-up while we investigate smoothing tunables. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Jordan: OK closing here after top-up applied and customer confirms no more 429s. Will follow up with docs PR.
